summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as the L3 forwarding router between node2 and node3. This required first building the missing point-to-point transit links (node1's eth1/eth2 had no IPs; node2/node3's second NIC enp8s0 was stuck waiting on DHCP that never arrives on this dhcp:false network). Assigned static addressing (node1 eth1=172.20.1.1/24 to node2 enp8s0=172.20.1.2/24; node1 eth2=172.20.2.1/24 to node3 enp8s0=172.20.2.2/24), added persistent routes on node2/node3 via nmcli, enabled IP forwarding on node1, and added an nftables FORWARD-hook table (inet transit_acl) that rejects tcp/23 with a TCP reset and explicitly accepts tcp/8080, leaving the default-accept policy untouched for all other traffic. Diagnosed and opened firewalld's local tcp/8080 port on node2 and node3 (their own host firewalls, not node1's ACL, were initially rejecting 8080 with an ICMP admin-prohibited reject from the destination host). Persisted node1's addressing/forwarding/ACL via a new systemd unit (transit-acl.service) since SONiC's own interfaces file only manages eth0. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot IDs plus working ACL/connectivity) on all three nodes, restarted each one at a time, polled until each came back, confirmed each boot_id changed, and re-verified full recovery of addressing, forwarding, the nftables ACL, and end-to-end TCP 8080/23 behavior plus untouched ICMP traffic in both directions.
actions_performed: Diagnosed topology: node1 (SONiC) had unaddressed eth1/eth2; node2/node3 (RHEL9) had enp8s0 stuck in DHCP 'connecting' on a dhcp:false transit network
Assigned static point-to-point IPs: node1 eth1=172.20.1.1/24 & eth2=172.20.2.1/24; node2 enp8s0=172.20.1.2/24; node3 enp8s0=172.20.2.2/24 via nmcli (persisted)
Added persistent routes: node2 172.20.2.0/24 via 172.20.1.1, node3 172.20.1.0/24 via 172.20.2.1, both with ipv4.never-default to avoid a spurious extra default route
Enabled net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding on node1 eth1/eth2
Verified baseline forwarding worked via ICMP before adding any ACL (falsify-before-committing)
Created nftables table inet transit_acl with a forward-hook chain: tcp dport 23 reject with tcp reset; tcp dport 8080 accept; policy accept (untouched for everything else)
Diagnosed 8080 initial failure as node2/node3's own firewalld rejecting inbound (ICMP admin-prohibited), not node1's ACL; opened 8080/tcp permanently in firewalld on both nodes
Verified bidirectional TCP 8080 succeeds, TCP 23 is refused (RST/connection refused), and ICMP passes untouched, before any restarts
Persisted node1's config across reboot via /usr/local/sbin/transit-acl-setup.sh + systemd unit transit-acl.service (enabled, runs after interfaces-config.service)
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service/data health) on all 3 nodes

Restarted node1 (reboot), polled until exec available, confirmed boot_id changed, verified eth1/eth2 addressing, forwarding sysctls, transit-acl.service active, and nft ruleset all recovered, then re-verified end-to-end connectivity
Restarted node2 (reboot), confirmed boot_id changed, verified enp8s0 addressing/route/firewalld port persisted, re-verified connectivity
Restarted node3 (reboot), confirmed boot_id changed, verified enp8s0 addressing/route/firewalld port persisted
Re-established test listeners and ran final bidirectional end-to-end verification: tcp/8080 works, tcp/23 refused, ping (untouched traffic) works, in both node2->node3 and node3->node2 directions

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: socat TCP tests both directions (node2->node3 and node3->node2) succeed, returning the echoed test string, both before and after the full node restart cycle

evidence.requirement: node1 refuses TCP port 23 between node2 and node3
evidence.summary: nftables rule 'tcp dport 23 reject with tcp reset' installed in node1's FORWARD hook; socat connection attempts to port 23 in both directions return 'Connection refused' (TCP RST) both before and after restarts

evidence.requirement: rest of forwarded traffic between node2 and node3 left untouched
evidence.summary: ICMP ping between node2 and node3 (via node1, ttl=63 confirming one router hop) succeeds throughout, unaffected by the tcp/23 reject and tcp/8080 accept rules since the transit_acl table's policy is accept and no other rules exist

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline captured boot_id 82b18f3b...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 2891b16a... confirms restart; transit-acl.service active, nft ACL table intact, eth1/eth2 re-addressed, and end-to-end 8080/23/ping tests pass after recovery

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline captured boot_id 377b5195...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 86797b9e... confirms restart; enp8s0 addressing/route/firewalld port persisted and 8080/23 tests pass after recovery

evidence.requirement: node3 mandatory restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline captured boot_id 583ddd53...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id a3f077e4... confirms restart; enp8s0 addressing/route/firewalld port persisted, and final bidirectional 8080/23/ping tests pass after recovery
